title: RFID Keg Tags — Stop Keg Loss, Real-Time Fleet View
summary: RFID keg tags enable automated tracking of beer kegs, wine barrels, beverage containers and reusable packaging through the entire distribution cycle. From filling line through distribution, retail delivery, tap room service and empty return. Reduce keg loss, optimise distribution routes and gain visibility into your container fleet.
heroPoints: Curved metal mount: antenna optimised for 350-500 mm diameter stainless steel keg surfaces.
IP68 + washdown rated: survives CIP (clean-in-place), caustic wash, steam cleaning and pressure washing.
10+ year service life. Ruggedised construction outlasts multiple keg refurbishment cycles.

brief.label: Chip options
brief.text: {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} / M730 / M775 (96-bit EPC, self-tune auto-adjust); NXP UCODE 8 / 9 (high-sensitivity -23 dBm); {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} (TID-locked serial). Memory: 96 / 128-bit EPC standard, 64 / 128-bit user memory for fill-date + batch payload.

brief.label: Frequency / air interface
brief.text: 860-960 MHz UHF RAIN per EPC Class 1 Gen 2 v2.1 / ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015. Regional: FCC Part 15 Subpart C 902-928 MHz, ETSI EN 302 208 865-868 MHz, ARIB STD-T107 916.7-920.9 MHz. Self-tune enabled for curved-metal detune compensation on 350-500 mm keg diameters.

brief.label: EPC / asset ID scheme
brief.text: GS1 GIAI-96 (Global Individual Asset Identifier) for returnable kegs per GS1 TDS 2.0; GRAI-96 (Global Returnable Asset Identifier) variant for sharing schemes; SSCC-96 at pallet level. EPCIS 2.0 custody events (ObjectEvent / TransactionEvent) for fill → load → deliver → empty-return legs.

brief.label: Construction
brief.text: ABS (UL 94 V-0) + epoxy-potted PCB, curved-surface on-metal antenna tuned to 304 / 316 stainless steel keg wall. Food-splash-zone adhesive backing per FDA 21 CFR §175.105 indirect food-contact and EU 10/2011 Annex I monomer compliance. IP68 / IP69K per IEC 60529 and ISO 20653.

brief.label: Dimensions & form factors
items: Curved chime clip-on (tool-less, 50 L Euro DIN 6647-2)

brief.label: Read range on stainless steel
brief.text: 2-4 m handheld (Zebra MC3390xR / Bluebird RFR900 / TSL 1128); 3-6 m chute-mounted fixed reader (Impinj R700 / Zebra FX9600); 4-8 m dock-portal (Impinj xArray / Keonn AdvanReader) for stacked kegs on returnable-pallet.

brief.label: Chemical & CIP resistance
brief.text: Caustic (NaOH 2% at 80 °C), peracetic acid (200 ppm at 40 °C), phosphoric acid (1% at 60 °C), chlorinated alkaline cleaners, nitric acid rinse; IPA and food-grade lubricants per NSF / H1 classification. Tested to 1,000+ CIP cycles without read-range degradation.

brief.label: Temperature range
brief.text: -30 to +120 °C service (covers blast-chiller to CIP); survives flash pasteurisation 72 °C / 15 min and tunnel pasteurisation up to 62 °C / 30 min; steam sterilisation 100 °C / 20 min. Freeze-thaw cycle tested per ASTM D1002.

brief.label: Attachment
brief.text: Option A: 3M VHB 5952 / 4991 industrial adhesive on upper chime per ASTM D3330 Method A (180° peel). Option B: stainless M4 rivet through chime (brewery-specified). Option C: tool-less clip-on for Euro DIN 6647-2 50 L keg. Surface prep per 3M IATD 70-0707-6069-4 (degrease + primer).

brief.label: Compliance framework
brief.text: GS1 General Specifications 24.x + GS1 TDS 2.0 + EPCIS 2.0 (ISO/IEC 19987:2015) · ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 · DIN 6647-1 / -2 (Euro keg dimensions) · BA (Brewers Association) Keg Management Best Practices · TTB 27 CFR Part 25 (US brewery operations) · HM Revenue & Customs Notice 226 (UK beer duty) · EU Directive 92/83/EEC (alcohol excise) · 3-A Sanitary Standards (wetted-surface food-contact) · EHEDG Doc 8 (hygienic design) · FDA 21 CFR §175.105 · EU Regulation 10/2011 · Directive 94/62/EC Packaging & Packaging Waste.

sections.title: Challenges breweries and beverage distributors face managing keg fleets without RFID
bullets: Craft breweries lose 5-10% of their keg fleet annually. A stainless steel keg costs $100-$200, so a 5,000-keg fleet losing 7% per year represents $35,000-$70,000 in asset write-offs before counting the beer left inside unreturned kegs.

Manual delivery receipts and paper logs cannot accurately track kegs across 50-200 retail accounts; discrepancies between the brewery's count and the distributor's count average 8-12% in breweries without automated tracking.

CIP (clean-in-place) wash and steam sterilization cycles destroy standard RFID labels within 10-20 cycles, forcing manual keg numbering via painted stencils that fade and create misidentification errors in the filling line.

Without fill-date tracking at the individual keg level, FIFO rotation is impossible. Kegs stored longest go undetected, resulting in off-flavored product reaching taps and customer complaints that damage brand reputation.

Identifying slow-returning retail accounts requires manual reconciliation of paper delivery receipts. A process that takes 2-3 days and often reveals kegs that have been at an account for 60-90 days with no action taken.

sections.title: How Proud Tek keg RFID tags solve fleet visibility and loss problems
bullets: IP68 / IP69K rated ABS housing (UL 94 V-0) with epoxy potting and curved on-metal antenna tuned to 304 / 316 stainless. Tested against standard CIP protocols (2% NaOH at 80 °C, 1% phosphoric acid at 60 °C, 200 ppm peracetic acid, steam sterilisation) to 1,000+ cycles without read-range degradation.

VHB 5952 or stainless-rivet mounting on the upper chime places the tag in the most protected zone of the keg, away from forklift impact and valve handling, delivering a 10+ year service life that outlasts multiple keg refurbishment cycles.

Delivery drivers use a handheld UHF reader (Zebra MC3390xR / Bluebird RFR900 / TSL 1128) to scan kegs on / off the truck at each retail stop — no infrastructure at the account required — emitting EPCIS 2.0 ObjectEvents / TransactionEvents that close the manual-receipt gap.

GS1 GIAI-96 pre-encoding at the filling line links each keg's globally unique returnable-asset ID to fill-date, beer style and batch number — enabling automated FIFO rotation in cold storage and proactive flagging of slow-moving inventory before best-by date.

Automated alerts flag retail accounts holding kegs past a customer-defined threshold (e.g., 30 days), wired into Kegshoe / Binwise / Ekos Keg Tracker / Arryved so targeted collection calls go out before kegs go missing entirely.

sections.title: Field-reference operating notes — GIAI-96 keg fleet RFID programmes
paragraphs: Loss-rate reduction, filling-line throughput gain, overdue-return detection and fleet right-sizing outcomes all vary with keg fleet size, route density, account mix, filling-line speed and the keg-management SaaS a brewery already runs, so what follows is the shape of the work integrators sequence on a GIAI-96 keg fleet deployment — not client-specific numbers. The sequencing is anchored to GS1 General Specifications 24.x, GS1 TDS 2.0 Tag Data Standard, EPCIS 2.0 (ISO/IEC 19987:2015) ObjectEvent / TransactionEvent / AggregationEvent, ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015, DIN 6647-1 / -2 Euro keg dimensions and Brewers Association Keg Management Best Practices.

Directional benchmarks published in the Brewers Association Keg Management Best Practices, UK BBPA keg-deposit-scheme annual reports and the GS1 Returnable Transport Items application guide describe keg loss moving from annual-attrition write-off territory toward fleet right-sizing once real-time custody is in place, filling-line identification moving from painted-stencil manual read to single-scan GIAI-96 capture, and overdue-account detection moving from weeks-after-the-fact paper reconciliation to real-time 30-day-threshold alerts — the direction programmes should expect, with magnitudes settled during the first full distribution cycle.

sections.title: The keg loss problem
paragraphs: Craft breweries and beverage distributors lose 5-10% of their keg fleet annually. A significant financial loss given that stainless steel kegs cost $100-$200 each. A brewery with 5,000 kegs losing 7% per year loses $35,000-$70,000 in keg assets alone, plus the cost of beer lost in unreturned kegs.

Without RFID, keg tracking relies on manual counts and delivery receipts — error-prone processes that cannot reliably track kegs across dozens of retail accounts. RFID enables automated, scan-at-speed operations: tag every keg with a GS1 GIAI-96 returnable-asset ID, scan at every handoff (filling, loading, delivery, return) and emit an EPCIS 2.0 custody event — so you know exactly where every keg is at all times.

sections.title: Keg lifecycle tracking
bullets: Filling line: scan kegs onto the filling line; EPCIS 2.0 ObjectEvent records fill date, beer style, batch number and best-by date against the GIAI-96.
Warehouse: bulk-scan palletised kegs in cold storage for real-time inventory by product and age; AggregationEvent links each keg to its SSCC-96 pallet.
Truck loading: scan kegs onto delivery trucks; system generates delivery manifest, route optimisation and TransactionEvent with the wholesaler GLN.
Retail delivery: scan kegs on / off at each delivery stop; system updates customer account, keg custody and ePOD via Microlise / Descartes / Samsara.
Empty returns: scan returned empties; system calculates keg turn time and identifies slow-returning accounts against the BA benchmark.
Maintenance: track keg age, wash count and mechanical condition; schedule refurbishment or retirement per 3-A Sanitary and EHEDG hygienic-design guidance.

faq.question: Will the tag survive our CIP (clean-in-place) process?
faq.answer: Yes. Our keg tags are specifically tested against standard brewery CIP protocols: caustic wash (2% NaOH at 80 °C), acid rinse (1% phosphoric acid at 60 °C), peracetic sanitise (200 ppm at 40 °C) and hot water rinse. The epoxy-potted construction and chemical-resistant ABS housing (UL 94 V-0) withstand 1,000+ CIP cycles without read-range degradation. The 3M VHB 5952 adhesive maintains bond strength per ASTM D3330 Method A through repeated CIP exposure, and the food-splash-zone adhesive backing is declared per FDA 21 CFR §175.105 and EU Regulation 10/2011.

faq.question: Where should the tag be mounted on the keg?
faq.answer: We recommend mounting on the upper chime (the rolled edge at the top of the keg) or on the side wall between the chimes. The chime location protects the tag from impacts during handling and stacking. The side-wall location provides better read range but is more exposed. Avoid mounting near the valve stem (handling damage) or the base (forklift contact). For DIN 6647-2 50 L Euro kegs we offer a tool-less clip-on variant that seats onto the upper chime without adhesive. We provide a mounting guide specific to your keg model (US Sanke D / G, Euro DIN 6647-1 / -2, UK Cask).

faq.question: Can we track kegs at retail locations without reader infrastructure?
faq.answer: Yes. Your delivery drivers can use a handheld UHF RFID reader (Zebra MC3390xR / Bluebird RFR900 / TSL 1128, smartphone-sized) to scan kegs on and off the truck at each stop. No infrastructure at the retail location is required. The scan data syncs to your keg tracking system (Kegshoe / Binwise / Ollie / Ekos Keg Tracker / Arryved) via cellular or Wi-Fi when the driver returns — emitting EPCIS 2.0 TransactionEvents against the wholesaler / retailer GLN. For large-volume accounts (bars, stadiums), a fixed portal reader (Impinj R700 / Zebra FX9600) at the loading dock automates the process entirely.
